h2: Ultrasonic testing in Seattle and Puget Sound: which assets need it and under which rules
html:
Ultrasonic testing in Seattle and Puget Sound: which assets need it and under which rules

Around Seattle, ultrasonic testing does three main jobs: wall-thickness and weld examination at the five Washington refineries, composite and metal inspection in the aerospace supply chain, and hull and structure gauging in Puget Sound shipyards. Hydro penstocks and pipelines add to it. Atlantis, based in Houston, sends UT crews to the site under procedures that an ASNT NDT Level III has reviewed, and quotes each scope separately.

Refinery corrosion programs. The state's refining capacity is all in western Washington: BP Cherry Point, about 227,000 barrels a day; HF Sinclair and Marathon at Anacortes; Phillips 66 at Ferndale; and U.S. Oil & Refining on the Tacoma tideflats. UT thickness readings at condition monitoring locations feed each owner's piping and vessel program. Phased array and TOFD cover weld examination, and automated corrosion mapping covers the areas where spot readings miss localized loss. Under WAC 296-104-100, unfired pressure vessels have biennial external inspection, and owner-user organizations may use NBIC or API 510 intervals instead. That makes thickness data part of the case for the interval the owner chooses. Atlantis provides the NDE and data review for those programs. It is not an Authorized Inspection Agency and does not sign as inspector of record.

Composites and aerospace. Boeing's Composite Wing Center in Everett builds the carbon fiber wings for the 777X. Toray's composite materials plant in the Tacoma area was set up in 1992 to supply Boeing. Composite structure is checked with pulse-echo and phased array UT for porosity, delamination and impact damage, and machined billets are checked for laminations before machining. Aerospace UT normally needs NAS 410 personnel and the prime's process approvals, so Atlantis confirms which scheme applies before any aerospace scope is accepted.

Hulls, ferries and naval vessels. Seattle-area dry docks include three at Vigor on Harbor Island and six at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard in Bremerton. Hull thickness gauging is measured against original scantlings and the class or Navy allowable loss. Washington State Ferries does most fleet maintenance at its Eagle Harbor facility on Bainbridge Island, but some repairs, inspections and preservation work still need a dry dock, so hull gauging is planned around docking slots.

Penstocks and pipelines. Seattle City Light's Ross, Diablo and Gorge dams on the Skagit River supply about a fifth of the utility's power. Their penstocks and steel water passages are surveyed for wall loss by UT during planned unit outages. On pipelines, the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission enforces safety rules on intrastate lines and inspects interstate lines in the state on PHMSA's behalf. Those lines include Olympic Pipe Line and Williams' Northwest Pipeline. UT at integrity digs and on girth-weld repairs is reported against 49 CFR Part 192 or 195.

  • Refinery CML thickness, PAUT and TOFD weld examination, corrosion mapping
  • Composite skins and spars: delamination, porosity and impact damage
  • Hull plating and tank structure gauged against allowable diminution
  • Penstock wall-loss surveys during hydro unit outages
  • Pipeline dig-site thickness and lamination checks

Next steps. The national service is described on ultrasonic testing. Weld coverage that needs phased array is on PAUT inspection in Seattle, and wall-loss surveys are on corrosion inspection in Seattle. Vessel programs are on pressure vessel inspection in Seattle. For technicians who want the method, NDT training for Seattle and UT training describe the route. Send the line list, drawings or gauging plan through the Seattle UT enquiry.
